subject: CobaltAI - short-log concession and ops next steps
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Kova <elena.kova@cobaltai.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 7 Jun 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: CobaltAI - short-log concession and ops next steps

Thanks for carving out time today — quick recap and suggested path forward from our end. High-level takeaways:

- CobaltAI asks: 0-retention for any end-user PII and a very short (<=48h) operational KV/log window for non-PII telemetry. Also preference for EU residency for any persistent data.
- Redwood constraints: we can support 0-persistence on model inputs via optional ephemeral routing for the affected routes; for short log windows we usually operate with a 72-hour short-log and an auditable pseudonymization step for anything classified as PII.

Proposal (pilot):
1) Pilot scope: route 2 sensitive endpoints through ephemeral mode (0-persistence for model inputs) for 30 days to validate quality.
2) Short-log window: agree to a 72-hour KV/log retention for non-PII telemetry during pilot; Redwood will apply stronger pseudonymization and token redaction for fields flagged as PII.
3) Residency: host pilot in US-West; if the pilot passes security review we can map to an EU region for production (timeline dependent on legal/infra).
4) Evidence: attaching SOC2-summary.pdf and a redacted data handling map; security questionnaire to follow.

Next steps:
- Elena/Tom: confirm whether the 72h short-log for non-PII is acceptable as an interim step (Elena: you mentioned procurement might need 48h; want to confirm).
- Redwood (Marissa & Stephanie): prepare a trimmed ops SLA showing the short-log handling and pseudonymization approach; provide the list of technical controls (KMS, audit logs, delete hooks) by EOD Wed.
- Schedule: propose a 30-minute follow-up on Thu 6/10 to align on scope and legal asks.

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
From: Elena Kova <elena.kova@cobaltai.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cobaltai.com>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CobaltAI - short-log concession and ops next steps

Thanks Nikhil — good summary. A couple clarifications from our security/procurement perspective: 

- Our preference is 0-persistence for any raw PII (names, SSN-like identifiers, raw email) across both dev and prod. We can accept a pilot where those calls are routed to an ephemeral path.
- On the short-log window: procurement will push back on 72h; they asked if we can get to 48h for non-PII KV/logs during the pilot. Their concern is lateral risk of telemetry.
- Residency: EU production is a hard requirement for our product team once we go live; pilot in US is fine if we get a clear plan and commitments for an EU cutover timeline.

If Redwood can deliver: (a) a documented pseudonymization approach that is reversible only via a customer-managed key, (b) a 48h short-log option for the pilot (or a clear path to get there within two weeks), and (c) SOC2 evidence (thanks for the attachment), then legal is willing to sign a short-form PoC agreement.

We also need to see any telemetry schemas so we can annotate fields that are PII vs. non-PII — I'll share an initial field map after this note.

Elena

--
Elena Kova
Head of Security & Privacy | CobaltAI
elena.kova@cobaltai.com | +44 20 7946 0301
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Kova <elena.kova@cobaltai.com>, Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 8 Jun 2027 12:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CobaltAI - short-log concession and ops next steps

Elena — appreciate the specifics, and totally understand procurement’s stance. Two quick notes and a counter-proposal that should be workable without compromising controls: 

1) 48h short-log: operationally feasible if we enable an additional automatic truncate job and prioritize the customer-managed KMS key for pseudonymization metadata. For the pilot we can offer a hardened 48h TTL on non-PII KV if CobaltAI signs the PoC by Friday.

2) Pseudonymization and key control: we can implement pseudonymization where the reversible mapping is encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key (we support popular providers and bring-your-own-key patterns). By default Redwood’s support team does not have access to the plaintext mapping without a documented escalation and audit. We'll include that in the security appendix.

3) EU residency plan: we can commit to an EU region cutover for production within 8–10 weeks post-pilot (this requires an SOW addendum and an infrastructure migration window).

Attachments and next artifacts from Redwood (Marissa / Stephanie):
- Security appendix (pseudonymization spec, KMS patterns, delete hooks)
- Short-form PoC + timeline draft
- Telemetry schema template (to help CobaltAI tag PII fields)

If you confirm acceptance of the 48h pilot TTL and the customer KMS approach, I’ll route the short-form PoC to legal and get the follow-up on the calendar. Proposed follow-up: Thu 6/10 10:00am PT.

Thanks — Nikhil

--
Nikhil Sharma
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Kova <elena.kova@cobaltai.com>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil.sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 9 Jun 2027 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CobaltAI - short-log concession and ops next steps

Looping in the ops/security artifacts Elena requested — see links below. We can meet the 48h pilot TTL with the following operational guarantees:

- Automatic truncate job: configuration applied at route level, audit trail to show truncation events.
- Pseudonymization: reversible mapping protected by customer-managed KMS; Redwood retention of mapping metadata limited to encrypted blobs only.
- Additional evidence: SOC2-summary.pdf (attached), and a redacted data map (attached).

Links:
- Pilot PoC draft: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Cobalt-POC-plan (commented)
- Telemetry schema template: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/telemetry-schema

Next steps from us: we will push the PoC short-form and the security appendix to your inbox by EOD today so your legal/procurement can review. Nikhil — please confirm the Thu 6/10 10:00am PT slot and I’ll add dial-in.

Cheers,
Marissa
